name: P2 · Unit 6 — System Software & Operating Systems
description: All topics so far (30 sets × 30 questions): System Software; OS Basics; Process Management & IPC; Process Synchronization; Threads; CPU Scheduling; Deadlocks; Memory Management; Virtual Memory; Storage Management; File Systems; I/O Systems; OS Security; Linux Operating System; Windows Operating System. More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

subjects.name: P2 · Unit 6 – System Software & Operating Systems

sets.name: 1 · Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers

questions.question: The role of a compiler in software development is

options.B: To convert high level code to machine code
options.C: To debug errors in the code

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A compiler translates the whole source program into machine (object) code. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q78

questions.question: A compiler is used for

options.A: Converting machine language to high level programming language
options.B: Converting high level programming language to machine language

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Translation goes from the high-level source to machine language. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q67

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are the example/examples of low-level programming language?
(a) Python
(b) Java
(c) C
(d) Machine language
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Machine (and assembly) language are low-level; KEA's key treats C as a high-level language. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q73

questions.question:
Match the following:
Generation of Languages: a) Second generation language  b) Third generation language  c) Fourth generation language  d) Fifth generation language
Example: i. Prolog  ii. FoxPro  iii. Assembler  iv. Pascal

options.A: a – iii, b – iv, c – ii, d – i
options.B: a – ii, b – iii, c – iv, d – i
options.C: a – iv, b – iii, c – ii, d – i
options.D: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: 2GL assembly, 3GL procedural languages such as Pascal, 4GL database/query tools such as FoxPro, 5GL logic languages such as Prolog. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered as an essential part of a computer system's hardware?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A compiler is system software, not hardware. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q68

questions.question: Which of the following helps Assembler to deal with branching code?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: The first pass builds the symbol table, so forward branch targets are known in the second pass. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: A symbol table in assembler contains

options.A: Mapping of variables and their memory addresses

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: The symbol table maps labels and symbols to addresses; opcodes are in the machine-opcode table. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Machine language is:

options.C: Binary instructions that the CPU executes directly; it is machine-dependent
options.D: A language that needs a compiler

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It needs no translation, but is very hard to write.

questions.question: Assembly language uses ____ and is translated into machine code by a(n) ____.

options.C: Mnemonics such as MOV and ADD; assembler

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each assembly statement usually maps to one machine instruction.

questions.question: A key difference between a compiler and an interpreter is that:

options.B: An interpreter produces an object file
options.C: A compiler executes line by line
options.D: A compiler translates the whole program before execution; an interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Compiled programs usually run faster; interpreters make debugging easier.

questions.question: An interpreter, on meeting an error in line 20 of a program:

options.C: Reports all errors before running anything

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A compiler reports errors for the whole program before any of it runs.

questions.question: The usual order of the phases of a compiler is:

options.A: Syntax analysis → lexical analysis → code generation → optimization
options.B: Semantic analysis → lexical analysis → parsing → code generation
options.C: Code generation → lexical analysis → parsing → optimization
options.D: Lexical analysis → syntax analysis → semantic analysis → intermediate code → code optimization → code generation

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The symbol table and error handler are used by all phases.

questions.question: The lexical analyzer (scanner) of a compiler produces:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: The parser (syntax analyzer) then builds a parse tree from the tokens.

questions.question: A cross-compiler is a compiler that:

options.A: Translates between two high-level languages only
options.B: Runs only on the target machine
options.D: Runs on one machine but produces code for a different machine

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Used to build software for embedded systems.

questions.question: In a two-pass assembler, the main task of pass 1 is to:

options.A: Assign addresses to all statements using the location counter and build the symbol table

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Pass 2 uses the symbol table to generate the object code.

questions.question: Using a label in an instruction before the label is defined is called a:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: One-pass assemblers handle it with back-patching.

questions.question: Assembler directives (pseudo-ops) such as START, END and EQU:

options.B: Give instructions to the assembler and do not themselves become machine instructions

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). DC/DS (or DB/DW) reserve or define storage.

questions.question: The table that holds the mnemonic opcodes and their machine codes in an assembler is the:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Labels and their addresses are in the symbol table.

questions.question: In an assembler, the location counter is used to:

options.D: Keep track of the address of the next instruction or data item

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: It is advanced by the length of each instruction.

questions.question: In Java, the compiler javac translates source code into:

options.A: Bytecode, which the Java Virtual Machine interprets or compiles just-in-time
options.D: Native machine code for one CPU only

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: This gives 'write once, run anywhere' portability.

questions.question: A program that converts machine code back into assembly language is a:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: A decompiler tries to recover high-level source.

questions.question:
Match the translator with its job:
a. Assembler
b. Compiler
c. Interpreter
d. Cross-compiler

1. Translates a whole high-level program into object code
2. Translates assembly language into machine code
3. Produces code for a different machine
4. Translates and runs statement by statement
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Translator matching is common in KEA papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Machine language is machine-dependent.
II. Assembly language programs run unchanged on every type of processor.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Assembly language is specific to a processor family.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A two-pass assembler handles forward references easily.
Reason (R): Pass 1 records the addresses of all labels in the symbol table.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Pass 2 can then fill in every address.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): An interpreter produces a separate object file that can be run later without the interpreter.
Reason (R): An interpreter translates and executes a program statement by statement.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: No object file is produced, so A is false.

questions.question: Which of these is a high-level language?
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: High-level languages are close to human language and machine-independent.

questions.question: Code optimization in a compiler aims to:

options.D: Make the target code faster or smaller without changing what the program does

questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: It works on intermediate code and/or target code.

questions.question: A missing semicolon in a C statement is detected during:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Type mismatches and undeclared variables are found in semantic analysis.

questions.question: Literals such as =F'5' in an assembly program are collected by the assembler in the:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: They are placed in a literal pool, e.g. at an LTORG statement.

questions.question: Writing a compiler for a language in that same language, and using a simpler version to compile it, is called:
questions.subject: Language Levels and Translators – Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers
questions.explanation: Most C compilers are themselves written in C.

sets.name: 2 · Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software

questions.question: What is the role of linker in compilation?

options.A: Translates source code to object code

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The linker combines object modules and libraries into one executable, resolving external references. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
In the process of macro expansion given:
S₁: lexical substitution implies replacement of a character string by another string during program generation
S₂: lexical substitution is employed to replace occurrences of formal parameters by some random values
Which of the following holds good?

options.A: Both S₁ and S₂ are true
options.B: Both S₁ and S₂ are false
options.C: S₁ is false and S₂ is true
options.D: S₁ is true and S₂ is false

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Formal parameters are replaced by the actual parameters of the call, not by random values (Dhamdhere). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/statements about software is/are correct?
(a) Software can be categorized into system software and application software
(b) System software includes operating system and device drives
(c) Application software includes software for tasks like word processing
(d) All system and application softwares are open-sources
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Much software is proprietary, so (d) is false. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q77

questions.question:
Match the following software with their respective categories
Software: (a) Microsoft Word  (b) Ubuntu Linux  (c) Eclipse IDE  (d) Norton Antivirus
Category: i) Application software  ii) Development software  iii) Utility software  iv) System software

options.A: a – iv, b – ii, c – iii, d – i
options.B: a – ii, b – i, c – iii, d – iv
options.C: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv
options.D: a – i, b – iv, c – ii, d – iii

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Word – application; Ubuntu – system (OS); Eclipse – development; Norton – utility. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q80

questions.question: Which of the following softwares is considered as application software?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Operating systems and firmware are system software. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of system software?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: An operating system is system software. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q75

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of application software?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: A web browser is an application program. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q82

questions.question: Static linking differs from dynamic linking because in static linking:

options.B: Library code is copied into the executable at link time; in dynamic linking shared libraries (.dll, .so) are linked at load or run time
options.D: Linking happens while the program is running

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Dynamic linking saves memory and lets libraries be updated without relinking.

questions.question: A loader is the system program that:

options.D: Places an executable program into main memory and prepares it for execution

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Loading is the last step before execution.

questions.question: The four functions of a loader are:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Classic textbook list (Donovan).

questions.question: Relocation means:

options.A: Copying a program to another computer
options.C: Adjusting the address-dependent parts of a program so it can run from a memory area other than the one assumed when it was translated

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Relocation bits or modification records tell the loader which words to adjust.

questions.question: An absolute loader:

options.B: Loads the program at the address fixed by the assembler, with no relocation

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Simple, but the programmer must know where the program will be loaded.

questions.question: The small program, stored in ROM/firmware, that starts loading the operating system when a computer is switched on is the:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It loads the boot loader or kernel from disk.

questions.question: A 'compile-and-go' (assemble-and-go) loader:

options.A: Places the translated code directly in memory and starts execution, without producing an object file

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Fast, but the program must be translated again every time it is run.

questions.question: Dynamic loading means that:

options.A: Loading is done by the compiler
options.B: All routines are loaded at start
options.D: A routine is loaded into memory only when it is first called

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Unused routines (e.g. error handlers) are never loaded.

questions.question: A macro is:

options.A: A subroutine called at run time with a return address
options.B: A named group of statements that is substituted (expanded) wherever its name is used

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Macro expansion is done by a macro processor (pre-processor) before translation.

questions.question: Compared with a subroutine call, a macro call:

options.C: Is expanded in-line at every use, making the program larger but avoiding call/return overhead
options.D: Keeps a single copy of the code

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Subroutines keep one copy and use CALL/RETURN.

questions.question: In assembler macro definitions, the body of the macro lies between the pseudo-ops:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The macro name and its formal parameters follow MACRO.

questions.question: The tables maintained by a two-pass macro processor include:

options.C: Macro Name Table (MNT), Macro Definition Table (MDT) and Argument List Array (ALA)

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: MNT points into the MDT for each macro.

questions.question: A debugger is a tool that helps a programmer to:

options.B: Find and fix errors using breakpoints, single-stepping and inspection of variables

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). e.g. gdb, or the debugger built into an IDE.

questions.question: A breakpoint in debugging is:

options.A: A marked point where program execution pauses so the programmer can examine its state
options.C: The last line of the program

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: Execution can then be continued or stepped.

questions.question:
Match the system program with its role:
a. Loader
b. Linker
c. Macro processor
d. Debugger

1. Places the program in memory for execution
2. Combines object modules and resolves external references
3. Expands macro calls
4. Helps locate errors with breakpoints
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). System-program matching appears in KSET papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A macro call is replaced by the macro body during expansion.
II. A subroutine's body is copied into the program at every call.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: A subroutine has a single copy reached by CALL.

questions.question: An external reference in an object module is:

options.A: A use of a symbol defined in another module, which the linker resolves

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: EXTRN / ENTRY (or extern / global) declarations mark such symbols.

questions.question: The output of a linker is typically a(n):
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The loader then brings the executable into memory.

questions.question: Utility software includes programs such as:

options.C: Antivirus, disk defragmenter, backup and file-compression tools

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Utilities help maintain and optimise the computer.

questions.question: A device driver is classified as:
questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: It lets the OS control a particular device.

questions.question: Conditional macro expansion (e.g. AIF and AGO in IBM assembler) allows:

options.A: Macros to be called at run time
options.D: Different statements to be generated depending on the macro's arguments

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The expansion-time variables and labels are processed by the macro processor.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Relocation is needed when a program is loaded at an address different from the one assumed during translation.
Reason (R): Address-sensitive instructions contain addresses computed from the assumed origin.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: The loader adds the difference to each such address.

questions.question: In system programming, a text editor is used to:

options.A: Create and modify source programs and other text files

questions.subject: Linkers, Loaders, Macros, Debuggers and Types of Software
questions.explanation: e.g. vi, nano, Notepad.

sets.name: 1 · Operating System Functions, Types and Structure

questions.question: A set of programs that controls the resources of a system and provides it to the users with an interface that is easier to use is called
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: The OS manages resources and offers a convenient interface. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q89

questions.question: Which one among the following is not a basic function of operating system?
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Virus protection is done by separate utility (antivirus) software. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Data Entry Operator P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary goal of an operating system?

options.A: To provide a platform for running applications

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: KEA's key: the OS is above all a resource manager. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q48

questions.question: Which one of the following is not true?

options.A: Kernel remains in the memory during the entire computer session.
options.B: Kernel is made of various modules which cannot be loaded in running operating system.
options.C: Kernel is the first part of the operating system to load into the memory during booting.
options.D: Kernel is the program that constitutes the central core of the operating system.

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Modern kernels such as Linux support loadable modules that can be added while the system runs. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q4

questions.question:
Match the following:
Operating System: a) Android  b) Windows Operating System  c) Linux  d) OS-X
Companies: i. Microsoft  ii. Google  iii. Apple  iv. Open source

options.A: a - i, b - ii, c - iii, d - iv
options.B: a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
options.C: a - iii, b - i, c - ii, d - iv
options.D: a - ii, b - iii, c - iv, d - i

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Android – Google; Windows – Microsoft; Linux – open source; OS X (macOS) – Apple. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q9

questions.question:
Which of the following is/are open source operating system?
(a) Linux  (b) Opensolaris
(c) BSD  (d) Android
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: All four are open source (Android's core is the Android Open Source Project). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q79

questions.question: An example of non-real-time systems is
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: E-mail has no strict deadlines; the others need guaranteed response times. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q74

questions.question: Which one of the following errors will be handled by the operating system?

options.D: Failure of power, connection and Lack of paper

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Error detection is an OS service covering hardware, I/O devices and the network. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: An operating system acts as:

options.A: An intermediary between the user and the computer hardware, and a manager of its resources

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Silberschatz: the OS is a resource allocator and a control program.

questions.question: In a batch operating system:

options.A: Strict deadlines must always be met
options.B: Similar jobs are grouped and run one after another without user interaction
options.D: Users interact with programs while they run

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Early mainframes used batch processing with punched cards.

questions.question: Multiprogramming means:

options.A: Running one program at a time
options.C: Keeping several jobs in memory so the CPU can switch to another job when one waits for I/O
options.D: Using many CPUs for one job

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Its aim is to increase CPU utilisation.

questions.question: A time-sharing (multitasking) system:

options.D: Switches the CPU among users' programs so quickly that each user gets fast interactive response

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each process receives a short time slice (quantum).

questions.question: A hard real-time system is one in which:

options.A: Missing a deadline is a system failure, e.g. an airbag controller or a pacemaker

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). In soft real-time systems, such as video streaming, an occasional missed deadline is tolerable.

questions.question: Privileged instructions, such as I/O and timer management, can be executed only in:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A mode bit in hardware tells which mode the CPU is in.

questions.question: In a monolithic kernel:

options.A: Most OS services run together in a single address space in kernel mode
options.B: Only message passing is in the kernel
options.D: Every service is a user program

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Traditional UNIX and Linux are monolithic (Linux with loadable modules).

questions.question: A microkernel design:

options.A: Puts all drivers in the kernel
options.C: Keeps only essential functions (IPC, basic scheduling, memory) in the kernel and runs other services in user space

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Examples: Mach, QNX, MINIX 3. It is more reliable but message passing adds overhead.

questions.question: In the layered approach to OS design:

options.A: All layers can call each other freely
options.B: Each layer uses only the services of the layers below it; layer 0 is the hardware

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's THE system used this structure.

questions.question: Windows NT-based systems and macOS are usually described as having a:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: They combine features of monolithic and microkernel designs.

questions.question: SPOOLING stands for:
questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Print jobs are spooled to disk and printed one by one.

questions.question: A timer interrupt is used by the OS mainly to:

options.C: Display the time on screen only
options.D: Prevent a user program from keeping the CPU forever

questions.subject: Operating System Functions, Types and Structure
questions.explanation: When the timer expires, control returns to the OS.

questions.question: In a time share operating system, when the time slot assigned to a process is completed, the process switches from current state to ____.

questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Speed-up ≤ 1 / (S + (1 − S)/N) = 1 / (0.25 + 0.375) = 1.6.

questions.question: If 50% of a program is serial, the maximum speed-up with any number of cores is:
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: As N → ∞, speed-up → 1/S = 1/0.5 = 2.

questions.question: Which is a programming challenge of multicore systems?

options.C: Dividing work into balanced tasks, splitting data, handling data dependencies, and testing and debugging

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Silberschatz lists identifying tasks, balance, data splitting, data dependency, testing and debugging.

questions.question: User-level threads are:

options.B: Managed by a thread library in user space, without kernel support
options.C: Managed directly by the OS kernel

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Kernel threads are supported and scheduled directly by the OS.

questions.question: In the many-to-one model, if one thread makes a blocking system call:

options.A: The entire process blocks, and threads cannot run in parallel on multicore systems
options.C: A new kernel thread is created

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). All user threads share one kernel thread.

questions.question: The one-to-one model, used by Linux and Windows:

options.B: Maps all user threads to one kernel thread
options.C: Allows only one thread per process
options.D: Maps each user thread to its own kernel thread – more concurrency, but creating a user thread needs a kernel thread

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It allows threads to run in parallel on multiple cores.

questions.question: The two-level model is a variation of the many-to-many model that also:

options.C: Allows a user thread to be bound to a particular kernel thread

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: It combines many-to-many multiplexing with one-to-one binding.

questions.question: Which model lets other threads keep running when one thread blocks AND lets threads run in parallel on several cores?
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Many-to-one fails on both counts.

questions.question: Running two hardware threads on one core, so the core can switch to the other thread during a memory stall, is called:
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: The OS sees each hardware thread as a logical CPU.

questions.question: The data structure that holds a thread's state (ID, registers, stack pointer, state) is the:
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: A process's PCB points to the TCBs of its threads.

questions.question: A busy web server creates a separate thread for each client request mainly to:

options.D: Serve many clients at once and stay responsive

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Thread pools are usually used instead of creating a thread per request.

questions.question:
Match the multithreading model with its mapping:
a. Many-to-one
b. One-to-one
c. Many-to-many
d. Two-level

1. Many user threads onto a smaller or equal number of kernel threads
2. Each user thread onto its own kernel thread
3. Many-to-many plus binding a user thread to a kernel thread
4. All user threads onto a single kernel thread
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Model matching is very common in KEA and KSET papers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Threads of the same process share code and data.
II. Threads of the same process share one stack.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Each thread has its own stack.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In the many-to-one model, threads cannot run in parallel on a multicore system.
Reason (R): Only one thread can access the kernel at a time, because all share a single kernel thread.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: That is the main limitation of the model.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Concurrency is impossible on a single-core system.
Reason (R): On a single core, the CPU switches among tasks so quickly that several tasks make progress.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: R describes concurrency on one core, so A is false.

questions.question: An advantage of user-level threads over kernel-level threads is that:

options.A: Switching between them needs no kernel-mode privileges, so it is fast
options.B: They always run in parallel on many cores
options.C: A blocking system call never blocks the process
options.D: The kernel schedules each of them separately

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Their main drawback is that one blocking call can block the whole process (in many-to-one).

questions.question: Kernel-level threads are:

options.C: Managed only by a user library
options.D: Created, scheduled and managed directly by the operating system

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Linux, Windows and macOS all support kernel threads.

questions.question: A word processor that checks spelling in one thread while the user types in another mainly shows the multithreading benefit of:
questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: The program stays interactive even while part of it is busy.

questions.question: On a multiprocessor, a single-threaded process can use:

options.A: Only one processor at a time

questions.subject: Thread Concepts, Multicore Programming and Multithreading Models
questions.explanation: Multithreading lets one process benefit from several cores (scalability).

sets.name: 2 · Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues

questions.question: The three main thread libraries in use today are:

options.C: POSIX Pthreads, Windows threads and Java threads

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Pthreads may be provided as a user-level or kernel-level library.

questions.question: POSIX Pthreads is:

options.B: A specification (IEEE 1003.1c) for thread behaviour, not an implementation

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Programs include <pthread.h>.

questions.question: In Pthreads, a new thread is created with:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). pthread_join() makes the caller wait for that thread to finish.

questions.question: A thread ends its own execution in Pthreads by calling:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Returning from the thread function also ends it.

questions.question: In the Windows API, threads are created with ____ and waited for with ____.
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: WaitForMultipleObjects() waits for several threads.

questions.question: In Java, a thread can be created by:

options.A: Extending the Thread class or implementing the Runnable interface

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The code to run goes in the run() method.

questions.question: In Java, a new thread actually begins executing when the program calls:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: start() creates the thread and the JVM then calls run() in it.

questions.question: Java's join() method makes the calling thread:

options.D: Wait until the target thread terminates

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: It is similar to pthread_join().

questions.question: Implicit threading means that:

options.A: Threads are created by hardware only
options.B: Compilers and run-time libraries, not the programmer, create and manage the threads
options.D: Each user writes their own scheduler

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Examples: thread pools, fork-join, OpenMP, Grand Central Dispatch, Intel TBB.

questions.question: A thread pool improves performance because:

options.B: It removes the need for a CPU
options.C: An existing idle thread serves a request faster than creating a new thread, and the number of threads is limited
options.D: It creates a new thread for every request

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Java offers thread pools through ExecutorService.

questions.question: OpenMP supports parallel programming in C, C++ and Fortran mainly through:

options.B: Compiler directives such as #pragma omp parallel

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: The run-time creates as many threads as there are cores.

questions.question: In the fork-join model:

options.A: A parent task forks child tasks that run in parallel and then joins (waits for and combines) their results

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Java's ForkJoinPool implements this model for recursive divide-and-conquer tasks.

questions.question: Grand Central Dispatch, which schedules blocks of work on dispatch queues, was developed by:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Serial queues run blocks in order; concurrent queues run them in parallel.

questions.question: If one thread of a multithreaded program calls fork(), and exec() is called immediately after, the better choice is:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). exec() replaces the whole process image, so duplicating every thread would be wasted work.

questions.question: In a multithreaded program, a signal may be delivered to:

options.A: The thread to which it applies, every thread, certain threads, or a thread designated to receive all signals

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Synchronous signals go to the thread that caused them.

questions.question: Terminating a thread before it has completed is called:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The thread to be cancelled is the target thread.

questions.question: In asynchronous cancellation:

options.A: The target thread checks periodically whether it should terminate
options.D: One thread immediately terminates the target thread

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). In deferred cancellation the target checks at safe cancellation points.

questions.question: The default cancellation type in Pthreads is:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: A thread can create a cancellation point by calling pthread_testcancel().

questions.question: Data that each thread keeps its own copy of, such as a per-thread transaction ID, is called:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: TLS values persist across function calls, unlike local variables.

questions.question: In many-to-many and two-level models, the intermediate data structure that appears to the user-thread library as a virtual processor is the:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). With scheduler activations, the kernel informs the library about events through upcalls.

questions.question: Linux creates both processes and threads with the system call:

options.D: clone(), whose flags decide how much the child shares with the parent

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Linux calls both 'tasks'.

questions.question: Windows keeps the data of each thread in the structures:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: TEB (thread environment block) lives in user space.

questions.question: The number of threads in a thread pool is usually chosen based on:

options.C: The number of CPUs, the amount of memory and the expected number of concurrent requests

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Some pools adjust their size dynamically.

questions.question: Two threads increment a shared counter without a lock. The result may be wrong because of:
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Shared data must be protected with a mutex or other synchronization.

questions.question:
Match the Pthreads function with its job:
a. pthread_create()
b. pthread_join()
c. pthread_exit()
d. pthread_cancel()

1. Terminates the calling thread
2. Waits for a thread to finish
3. Requests termination of a target thread
4. Creates a new thread
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). API matching is common in KEA papers.

questions.question:
Match the implicit-threading technique with its description:
a. Thread pool
b. OpenMP
c. Fork-join
d. Grand Central Dispatch

1. Threads created at start-up that wait for work
2. Compiler directives that mark parallel regions
3. Apple's dispatch queues
4. Parent forks subtasks and later joins their results
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Implicit-threading approaches.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Deferred cancellation lets a thread terminate at a safe point.
II. Asynchronous cancellation is always safe for shared data.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Asynchronous cancellation may leave resources or shared data in an inconsistent state.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Thread pools usually serve requests faster than creating a new thread for each request.
Reason (R): An existing thread is reused instead of being created and destroyed.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Creation and destruction costs are avoided.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Calling run() directly on a Java Thread object starts a new thread.
Reason (R): The start() method creates a new thread, which then calls run().

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: Calling run() directly runs it in the current thread, so A is false.

questions.question: Intel Threading Building Blocks (TBB) is:

options.A: A C++ template library for designing parallel applications

questions.subject: Thread Libraries, Implicit Threading and Threading Issues
questions.explanation: It is another example of implicit threading.

sets.name: 1 · Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF

questions.question: Which of the following is not a CPU scheduling algorithm?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Rollback is a recovery action, not a scheduling algorithm. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Computer Operator P2 · Q71

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of First Come First Served (FCFS) scheduling algorithm?

options.A: It leads to starvation of processes
options.B: It may cause high waiting time for processes
options.C: It is a preemptive scheduling algorithm
options.D: It requires knowledge of burst times.

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Short jobs may wait behind a long one (convoy effect), so average waiting time can be high. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q35

questions.question:
Consider the following processes and their burst times
Process – Burst Time: P₁ – 5, P₂ – 8, P₃ – 3, P₄ – 6, P₅ – 7
If the CPU scheduling is performed using Shortest Job First (SJF) (non-preemptive), then what will be the correct sequence of processes executed?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Shortest burst first: 3, 5, 6, 7, 8. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q36

questions.question:
In SRT process scheduling algorithm, the arrival & execution time of the four processes are as follows.
Arrival time – Execution time – Process: 0 – 20 – P₁; 15 – 25 – P₂; 30 – 10 – P₃; 45 – 15 – P₄
What will be the process 'P₂' total waiting time?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: P₁ runs 0–20; P₂ runs 20–30, is preempted by P₃ (30–40), resumes 40–50; P₄ runs 50–65. P₂ waits (20 − 15) + (40 − 30) = 15. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q14

questions.question:
Consider a single processor system with four processes A, B, C and D represented as given below, where for each process the first value is its arrival time and second value is its CPU burst time
A(0, 10), B(2, 6), C(4, 3) and D(6, 7)
Which of the following options gives the average waiting time when preemptive Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) and the Non-Preemptive Shortest Job First (NP-SJF) CPU scheduling algorithms are applied to the process?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: SRTF: A 0–2, B 2–4, C 4–7, B 7–11, D 11–18, A 18–26 → waits 16, 3, 0, 5 → 6. NP-SJF: A 0–10, C 10–13, B 13–19, D 19–26 → waits 0, 11, 6, 13 → 7.5. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Consider the following set of processes that arrive at time 0 with length of the CPU burst time given in milliseconds: P1 = 26, P2 = 4, P3 = 5. What is the average waiting time for the processes that arrive in the orders P1, P2, P3 and P2, P1, P3 under FCFS policy?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Order 1: waits 0, 26, 30 → 56/3 ≈ 18.67. Order 2: waits 0, 4, 30 → 34/3 ≈ 11.33. Option 2 is the closest (truncated) value. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: ____ is invoked when there is a need to perform process scheduling, that is when a process from the ready queue is to be selected for dispatching to the CPU.
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: The short-term (CPU) scheduler picks the next ready process for the CPU. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Process execution alternates between periods of computation and waiting for I/O. This is called the:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: CPU-bound processes have a few long bursts; I/O-bound processes many short ones.

questions.question: In preemptive scheduling:

options.A: The CPU can be taken away from a running process, e.g. when a higher-priority process arrives or a time slice ends
options.B: A process keeps the CPU until it finishes or blocks

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Non-preemptive (cooperative) scheduling switches only when the running process terminates or waits.

questions.question: A good CPU scheduling algorithm tries to:

options.C: Maximise CPU utilisation and throughput; minimise turnaround, waiting and response times

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The five classic scheduling criteria.

questions.question: Turnaround time of a process is:

options.A: Time of first response − arrival time

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Waiting time = turnaround time − burst time.

questions.question: A process arrives at time 2, has a CPU burst of 5 and completes at time 10. Its waiting time is:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Turnaround = 10 − 2 = 8; waiting = 8 − 5 = 3.

questions.question: Response time, important in interactive systems, is the time from submission of a request until:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: It is different from turnaround time.

questions.question: The number of processes that complete their execution per unit time is called:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Higher throughput means more work done.

questions.question: Three processes arrive at time 0 in the order P1, P2, P3 with bursts 24, 3 and 3 ms. Under FCFS the average waiting time is:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Waits 0, 24, 27 → 51/3 = 17. If the order were P2, P3, P1 the average would be (0 + 3 + 6)/3 = 3.

questions.question: The 'convoy effect' – many short processes waiting behind one long CPU-bound process – is typical of:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It lowers CPU and device utilisation.

questions.question: Which scheduling algorithm gives the minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). SJF is provably optimal for average waiting time.

questions.question: Processes P1–P4 arrive at time 0 with bursts 6, 8, 7 and 3. Under non-preemptive SJF the average waiting time is:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF

questions.question: The main practical difficulty with SJF is that:

options.A: The length of the next CPU burst is not known in advance and must be predicted

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Predicted with exponential averaging: τ(n+1) = α·t(n) + (1 − α)·τ(n).

questions.question: Using exponential averaging with α = 0.5, a previous prediction τ = 10 ms and an actual last burst t = 6 ms, the next predicted burst is:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF

questions.question: Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) is:

options.A: Round Robin with a small quantum
options.D: The non-preemptive version of priority scheduling

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: A newly arrived process with a shorter remaining time preempts the running one.

questions.question: A drawback of SJF and SRTF is that:

options.A: They have very high context-switch overhead in all cases
options.C: They cannot be used in batch systems
options.D: Long processes may starve if short ones keep arriving

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Ageing can be used to prevent starvation.

questions.question: The simplest CPU scheduling algorithm to implement, using a FIFO queue, is:
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: New processes join the tail; the CPU goes to the head.

questions.question:
Match the scheduling measure with its definition:
a. Turnaround time
b. Waiting time
c. Response time
d. Throughput

1. Processes completed per unit time
2. Time until the first response
3. Total time spent in the ready queue
4. Completion time − arrival time
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Criteria matching is common.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. SJF minimises the average waiting time.
II. FCFS is a preemptive algorithm.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: FCFS is non-preemptive.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): FCFS scheduling may cause the convoy effect.
Reason (R): Short processes have to wait behind a long CPU-bound process.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: That is the definition of the convoy effect.

questions.question: A Gantt chart in CPU scheduling shows:

options.D: Which process runs on the CPU during each interval of time

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Numerical scheduling questions are solved by drawing one.

questions.question: Which scheduling algorithm can be either preemptive or non-preemptive?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Priority scheduling can also be either.

questions.question: In a non-preemptive scheduler, a context switch to another process happens only when the running process:

options.A: Terminates or switches to the waiting state
options.C: Is interrupted by a higher-priority arrival

questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Windows 3.x and early Mac OS used cooperative (non-preemptive) scheduling.

questions.question: Which criterion matters MOST for an interactive (time-sharing) user?
questions.subject: Scheduling Criteria, FCFS, SJF and SRTF
questions.explanation: Users want the system to react quickly.

sets.name: 2 · Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling

questions.question: There are 10 different processes running on a workstation. Idle processes are waiting for an input event in the input Queue. Busy processes are scheduled with Round Robin time sharing method. Which of the following quantum times is the best value for small response times, if the processes have a short run time, eg., less than 10 ms?
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: A quantum just above the typical burst lets most processes finish in one slice while keeping response time small. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q1

questions.question:
Which of the following statement/statements is/are true?
I. Shortest remaining time first scheduling may cause starvation.
II. Preemptive scheduling may cause starvation.
III. Round Robin is better than FCFS in terms of response time.
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: All three are true. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q2

questions.question:
Match the following with respect to scheduling algorithm
a) FCFS  b) SJF  c) RR  d) Priority Scheduling
i. Allocation based on the lowest CPU burst time  ii. According to the arrival time of the process, the CPU is allocated.  iii. According to the priority  iv. According to the order of the process arrives with fixed time quantum.

options.A: a - i, b - iii, c - iv, d - ii
options.B: a - ii, b - i, c - iv, d - iii
options.C: a - iv, b - iii, c - i, d - ii
options.D: a - iv, b - ii, c - iii, d - i

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: FCFS – arrival order; SJF – shortest burst; RR – arrival order with a fixed quantum; Priority – by priority. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q13

questions.question:
Considering the following statements, choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): The Round Robin (RR) scheduling algorithm is considered a preemptive scheduling algorithm.
Reason (R): The Round Robin (RR) algorithm allocates a fixed time slice to each process in the ready queue before moving to the next process.

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: When the time slice expires the process is preempted – that is why RR is preemptive. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q41

questions.question:
In a priority scheduling algorithm, which of the following are true?
a. Higher priority processes are executed first
b. Starvation can occur if low-priority processes are never executed
c. Equal priority processes are executed in the order they arrive.
d. Preemption is mandatory in priority scheduling
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Priority scheduling can be preemptive or non-preemptive, so (d) is false; ties are broken FCFS. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q46

questions.question: Which scheduling algorithm is used in realtime systems to ensure that critical processes meet their deadlines?
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: EDF gives the highest priority to the process with the nearest deadline. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q50

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
(a) FCFS Scheduling
(b) SJF Scheduling
(c) Priority Scheduling
(d) RR Scheduling
(i) Shortest burst time
(ii) Indefinite Blocking
(iii) Time slice
(iv) Convoy effect

options.A: a – ii, b – iii, c – i, d – iv
options.B: a – iii, b – ii, c – iv, d – i
options.C: a – iv, b – i, c – ii, d – iii
options.D: a – i, b – iii, c – ii, d – iv

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: FCFS suffers the convoy effect, SJF picks the shortest burst, priority scheduling risks starvation, RR uses a time quantum. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In Silberschatz's convention for priority scheduling:

options.B: A larger number always means higher priority
options.D: A smaller priority number means a higher priority

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Conventions differ between systems, so read each question carefully.

questions.question: Starvation of low-priority processes in priority scheduling is solved by:

options.D: Ageing – gradually increasing the priority of waiting processes

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Ageing is the standard answer.

questions.question: Round Robin scheduling is designed especially for:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is FCFS with preemption after each time quantum.

questions.question: In Round Robin, if the time quantum is made very large, the algorithm behaves like:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). If it is very small, context-switch overhead dominates.

questions.question: Processes P1, P2, P3 arrive at time 0 with bursts 24, 3 and 3 ms. With Round Robin and quantum 4 ms, the average waiting time is about:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Order P1(0–4), P2(4–7), P3(7–10), P1(10–30): waits 6, 4, 7 → 17/3 ≈ 5.67.

questions.question: A rule of thumb for choosing the RR time quantum is that:

options.A: The quantum should be longer than every burst
options.B: About 80% of CPU bursts should be shorter than the quantum
options.D: The quantum should equal the context-switch time

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Then most processes finish in one quantum without too many switches.

questions.question: In a multilevel queue scheduler:

options.A: Processes freely move between queues based on behaviour
options.B: The ready queue is split into separate queues (e.g. foreground interactive, background batch), and a process stays permanently in one queue
options.D: Each process has its own CPU

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each queue may use its own algorithm, e.g. RR for foreground and FCFS for background.

questions.question: A multilevel feedback queue scheduler differs from a multilevel queue because:

options.D: Processes can move between queues – CPU-hungry processes move down, long-waiting ones move up

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is the most general – and most complex – scheduling scheme.

questions.question: Rate-monotonic scheduling for periodic real-time tasks:

options.C: Assigns static priorities – the shorter the period, the higher the priority
options.D: Assigns priorities by nearest deadline dynamically

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). EDF assigns dynamic priorities by deadline.

questions.question: The worst-case CPU-utilisation bound for rate-monotonic scheduling of two tasks is about:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: n(2^(1/n) − 1): about 83% for n = 2, tending to 69% as n grows. EDF can, in theory, reach 100%.

questions.question: Processor affinity means:

options.A: Running a process on all processors at once
options.B: Giving a process the highest priority
options.C: Keeping a process on the same processor to benefit from its warm cache

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Soft affinity tries to do this; hard affinity guarantees it.

questions.question: In multiprocessor scheduling, moving tasks from an overloaded processor to an idle one is:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: It may conflict with processor affinity.

questions.question: Linux's default scheduler for normal tasks, the Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS), keeps runnable tasks in a:

options.B: Red-black tree ordered by virtual runtime (vruntime)

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The task with the smallest vruntime runs next.

questions.question: Windows schedules threads using a priority scheme with:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Levels 16–31 are the real-time class; 1–15 the variable class.

questions.question: Lottery scheduling gives each process tickets and picks a random ticket. It is an example of:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: A process with more tickets gets more CPU time on average.

questions.question: In thread scheduling, competition among the user threads of the same process (many-to-one / many-to-many models) is called:
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Kernel threads compete with all threads in the system (SCS).

questions.question:
Match the scheduler with its key idea:
a. Rate-monotonic
b. Earliest Deadline First
c. Linux CFS
d. Multilevel feedback queue

1. Fair share using a red-black tree of virtual runtimes
2. Processes move between queues according to behaviour
3. Dynamic priority by the nearest deadline
4. Static priority by the shortest period
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Advanced scheduling matching.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Ageing prevents starvation in priority scheduling.
II. Round Robin with a very large quantum behaves like FCFS.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Both are standard results.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A very small Round Robin quantum makes the system inefficient.
Reason (R): Context-switch overhead becomes large compared with useful work.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: The quantum should be large compared with the context-switch time.

questions.question: In symmetric multiprocessing (SMP) scheduling:

options.A: Each processor is self-scheduling, from a common or private ready queue
options.B: Only one master processor schedules all others
options.D: Scheduling is done by hardware alone

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Asymmetric multiprocessing has one master processor doing all scheduling.

questions.question: Which statement about preemptive priority scheduling is TRUE?

options.B: It cannot be used in real-time systems
options.C: It is the same as FCFS
options.D: A newly arrived higher-priority process immediately takes the CPU from a lower-priority running process

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: Non-preemptive priority would only put the new process at the head of the ready queue.

questions.question: In Round Robin with n processes in the ready queue and quantum q, no process waits more than:

options.A: (n − 1) × q time units before its next quantum

questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: This bounded wait is why RR gives good response times.

questions.question: Which algorithm is most suitable for a batch system where all job lengths are known in advance and average waiting time must be minimal?
questions.subject: Priority, Round Robin, Multilevel, Multiprocessor and Real-time Scheduling
questions.explanation: SJF is optimal for average waiting time.

sets.name: 1 · Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention

questions.question: A process needs to release all resources before it makes any requests for another resources. Select the true statement from the following.

options.A: Deadlock cannot occur, but starvation can occur
options.B: Both deadlock and starvation can occur
options.C: Neither deadlock nor starvation can occur
options.D: Deadlock can occur but starvation cannot occur

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: This breaks the hold-and-wait condition, so deadlock is impossible, but a process may wait indefinitely for popular resources. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Sr/Jr Programmer P2 · Q16

questions.question: Which is the correct sequence of steps involved in resolving deadlock using the resource allocation graph method?

options.A: Check for cycles → Identify deadlocked processes → Release Resources
options.B: Identify deadlocked processes → Check for cycles → Release Resources
options.C: Check for cycles → Release Resources → Identify deadlocked processes
options.D: Identify deadlocked processes → Release Resources → Check for cycles

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: A cycle reveals the deadlocked processes, whose resources are then released (by aborting or preempting). (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q38

questions.question: A deadlock is a situation in which:

options.A: A process is waiting for I/O to complete
options.B: The CPU is idle because no process exists
options.C: Each process in a set waits for an event that only another process in the set can cause

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). None of the processes can proceed.

questions.question: The four necessary conditions for deadlock (Coffman conditions) are:

options.A: Mutual exclusion, starvation, ageing and paging
options.B: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption and circular wait
options.C: Hold and wait, preemption, spooling and swapping
options.D: Circular wait, thrashing, paging and segmentation

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). All four must hold at the same time for a deadlock.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: The condition is 'no preemption'.

questions.question: In a resource-allocation graph, an edge Pi → Rj means:

options.C: Resource Rj is assigned to Pi
options.D: Process Pi has requested resource Rj (request edge)

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Rj → Pi is an assignment edge.

questions.question: If a resource-allocation graph has no cycle, then:
questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A cycle is necessary for deadlock.

questions.question: If every resource type has exactly one instance, a cycle in the resource-allocation graph:

options.D: Implies that a deadlock has occurred

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). With several instances per type, a cycle is necessary but not sufficient.

questions.question: The methods of handling deadlocks are:

options.B: Prevention, avoidance, detection and recovery, or ignoring the problem

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Ignoring the problem (the 'ostrich algorithm') is what most general-purpose OSs, including Linux and Windows, actually do.

questions.question: Deadlock prevention works by:

options.A: Granting requests only in safe states
options.C: Ensuring that at least one of the four necessary conditions can never hold

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: Avoidance uses extra information to stay in safe states.

questions.question: The mutual-exclusion condition generally cannot be denied for:

options.C: Intrinsically non-sharable resources such as a printer or a mutex

questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: Spooling a printer is one way around it.

questions.question: Requiring a process to request all its resources before it begins execution prevents deadlock by denying:
questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Drawbacks: low resource utilisation and possible starvation.

questions.question: Imposing a total ordering of resource types and requiring processes to request them in increasing order prevents:
questions.subject: Deadlock Conditions, Resource-allocation Graph and Prevention
