Consider the statements:
I. SSTF always gives the minimum possible total head movement.
II. SSTF may starve requests far from the head.
questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: SSTF is greedy and not always optimal; it can also starve distant requests.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): FCFS disk scheduling is fair.
Reason (R): Requests are serviced in the order in which they arrive.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: It is fair but usually not fast.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): C-SCAN gives a more uniform waiting time than SCAN.
Reason (R): C-SCAN serves requests in both directions of arm movement.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: C-SCAN serves requests in one direction only and jumps back; that is why waiting times are more uniform.

questions.question:
Match the disk-scheduling algorithm with its description:
a. FCFS
b. SSTF
c. SCAN
d. C-LOOK

1. Closest request first
2. Order of arrival
3. End to end and back
4. One direction, up to the last request, then jump
questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A common matching question.

questions.question: Linux's 'deadline' I/O scheduler keeps separate read and write queues mainly to:

options.D: Prevent starvation by giving each request an expiry time

questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: Reads are given shorter deadlines because processes usually block on them.

questions.question: Head at 100, requests 55, 58, 39, 18, 90, 160, 150, 38, 184. The first request served under SSTF is:
questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: 90 is 10 cylinders away – the nearest.

questions.question: Which factor makes FCFS a good choice for SSDs and NVM devices?

options.A: Access time does not depend on the position of the data
options.B: SSDs have very long seek times

questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Linux uses the NOOP (none) scheduler for many NVM devices.

questions.question: Disk bandwidth is defined as:

options.B: Total bytes transferred divided by the total time between the first request and completion of the last transfer
options.D: The seek time of one request

questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: Scheduling improves both access time and bandwidth.

questions.question: If requests arrive mostly for cylinders near the middle of the disk, which algorithm is least likely to help?
questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: FCFS ignores the head position completely.

questions.question: Head at 53; queue 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67; the head moves towards higher cylinders under C-LOOK. The order of service is:
questions.subject: Disk Scheduling – FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, C-SCAN, LOOK
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). After 183 the head jumps back to the lowest pending request (14) and continues upwards.

sets.name: 1 · File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing

questions.question:
The information that are associated with an open file
(a) Creating a file, Access rights
(b) Opening a file, File pointer
(c) File pointer, File open count
(d) Disk location of the file, Access rights
Which of the aforementioned statements are correct?
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Silberschatz: file pointer, file-open count, disk location and access rights are kept for each open file. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which is an important file used by the system and should not be altered or removed from the disk?
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: System files (marked with the S attribute in Windows) are needed for the OS to run. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The command used to change file permission is
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: In Windows/MS-DOS, attrib sets the read-only, hidden, system and archive attributes; fdisk partitions disks. (On Linux the command is chmod.) (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: When a share name ends in a dollar sign, it is a ____ share
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: In Windows, a share such as C$ or ADMIN$ does not appear when users browse the network. (Official answer: KEA final key, GTTC recruitment 2024.)

questions.question: A file is best defined as:

options.D: A named collection of related information recorded on secondary storage

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It is the smallest allotment of logical secondary storage.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT usually a file attribute?

options.B: The CPU burst time of the file

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Attributes include name, identifier, type, location, size, protection, time and user ID.

questions.question: Reading records one after another in order, as on a tape, is called:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). read_next() and write_next() move the file pointer forward.

questions.question: Access that lets a program read or write any numbered block of a file in no particular order is:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Databases need direct access.

questions.question: Indexed sequential access (ISAM) uses:

options.A: An index to find the block, then sequential search within it

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Large files may use a multilevel index.

questions.question: The directory structure in which each user has his own directory under a master file directory is:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It isolates users but makes sharing hard.

questions.question: Which directory structure allows a file or subdirectory to be shared by appearing in more than one directory, without cycles?
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Sharing is done with links.

questions.question: In a tree-structured directory, a path that begins at the root is called:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A relative path begins at the current directory, e.g. ../docs.

questions.question: Attaching a file system to the existing directory tree at a given directory is called:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: The directory is the mount point, e.g. /mnt/usb on Linux.

questions.question: In UNIX, file access rights are given for three classes of users:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each class has read, write and execute bits – e.g. rwxr-x--- = 750.

questions.question: The octal permission 754 on a UNIX file means:

options.B: Owner r-x, group rwx, others r--
options.C: Owner rwx, group r-x, others r--
options.D: Owner rw-, group r-x, others r--

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing

questions.question: A file type is commonly indicated in Windows by:

options.D: The file-name extension, such as .exe or .docx

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: UNIX instead uses a 'magic number' at the start of some files.

questions.question: Consistency semantics that make writes to an open file visible immediately to other users who have it open are:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Session semantics (AFS) show changes only after the file is closed.

questions.question: A file that, once declared shared by its creator, cannot be modified is called:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Its name may not be reused and its contents cannot change.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A hard link points directly to the file's inode.
II. A symbolic (soft) link stores the path name of the target file.
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Deleting the target leaves a dangling symbolic link, but a hard link keeps the data alive.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A two-level directory solves the name-collision problem between different users.
Reason (R): Each user has a separate user file directory.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Two users can then have files with the same name.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): In a single-level directory, two users can have files with the same name.
Reason (R): A single-level directory keeps all files in one directory.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Since all files share one directory, names must be unique.

questions.question: Which of the following operations on a file needs the file to be searched in the directory first?

options.B: Read from an already opened file using its file handle
options.D: Reposition within an already opened file

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). open() searches the directory once and returns an index into the open-file table.

questions.question: A lock that allows several processes to read a file at once but only one to write is:

options.B: Shared lock for readers and exclusive lock for writers

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Windows uses mandatory locks; UNIX uses advisory locks.

questions.question:
Match the access method with an example:
a. Sequential
b. Direct
c. Indexed

1. Finding a book via a catalogue
2. Reading a tape
3. Airline seat record by number
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Indexed access uses an index like a library catalogue.

questions.question: The OS keeps a table with information about all open files. The file is removed from this table when:

options.B: The file-open count drops to zero after the last close

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each process also has its own per-process open-file table.

questions.question: In MS-DOS, the command used to create a new directory is:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: CD changes, RD removes and DIR lists directories.

questions.question: The Windows file system that supports file permissions, encryption, compression and journaling is:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). FAT32 is simpler and is still used on USB drives; exFAT removes FAT32's 4 GB file-size limit.

questions.question: The maximum size of a single file on a FAT32 volume is:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: exFAT and NTFS allow much larger files.

questions.question: Which of these is a garbage-collection problem specific to general-graph directories?

options.B: Cycles can make files unreachable while their reference counts are not zero

questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Acyclic graphs avoid this by forbidding links to directories.

questions.question: The protection approach that associates with each file a list of users and their allowed operations is:
questions.subject: File Concept, Access Methods, Directories, Mounting and Sharing
questions.explanation: Condensed versions use owner, group and universe classes.

sets.name: 2 · Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery

questions.question:
Which of the following file allocation methods would be efficient when dealing with a large number of small sized files?
i. Contiguous allocation
ii. Linked allocation
iii. Indexed allocation
iv. File Allocation Table (FAT)
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: The official key prefers linked allocation and FAT, which waste no space on an index block for each small file. (Official answer: KEA final key, Legislative Council Secretariat exam 2024.)
questions.source: Legislative Council 2024 Junior Console Operator P2 · Q44

questions.question: Contiguous allocation of disk space for files suffers from:

options.C: External fragmentation and difficulty in growing files

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). It gives excellent sequential and direct access, as on CDs.

questions.question: In contiguous allocation, a file is described in the directory by:

options.C: A chain of pointers in each block

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Block b + i is the i-th block of a file starting at b.

questions.question: Linked allocation of files gives:

options.C: No external fragmentation, but direct access is slow

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: To reach block i, the chain from the first block must be followed.

questions.question: The File Allocation Table (FAT) used by MS-DOS is a variation of:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The chain of pointers is kept in a table at the start of the volume rather than in the blocks.

questions.question: Indexed allocation brings all the pointers of a file together into:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Direct access is fast; small files waste most of the index block.

questions.question: A UNIX inode has 12 direct pointers and single, double and triple indirect pointers. With 4 KB blocks and 4-byte pointers, a single indirect block holds:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 4096 / 4 = 1024 block addresses.

questions.question: With 4 KB blocks, 4-byte block pointers and 12 direct pointers, the largest file reachable with only the direct and single-indirect pointers is:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery

questions.question: The UNIX inode scheme that combines direct and multi-level indirect blocks is called:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Small files need only direct blocks, so access is fast.

questions.question: A bit vector (bitmap) for free-space management uses one bit per:

options.C: Disk block, 1 = free and 0 = allocated (Silberschatz convention)

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: It is simple and makes it easy to find runs of free blocks.

questions.question: A 1 TB disk with 4 KB blocks needs a free-space bitmap of about:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). 2^40 / 2^12 = 2^28 blocks → 2^28 bits = 2^25 bytes = 32 MB.

questions.question: Keeping the address of the first free block, with each free block pointing to the next, is the free-space method called:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Grouping stores n free-block addresses in the first free block; counting stores (address, count) pairs.

questions.question: The structure on disk that contains the details of a volume – number of blocks, block size, free-block count – is called the superblock in UNIX and the ____ in NTFS.
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The boot control block holds the information needed to boot from the volume.

questions.question: In the layered file system design, the layer that translates logical block addresses to physical block addresses is the:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Layers: application → logical file system → file-organisation module → basic file system → I/O control → devices.

questions.question: A directory implemented as a linear list of file names has the disadvantage of:

options.D: Slow linear search for a file

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A hash table speeds up search but must handle collisions.

questions.question: Keeping frequently used directory entries and disk blocks in main memory to speed up the file system uses a:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: A unified buffer cache avoids double caching of memory-mapped files.

questions.question: A journaling (log-structured) file system records metadata changes in a log first so that:

options.D: The file system can be recovered quickly after a crash

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). ext4, NTFS and XFS are journaling file systems; fsck-style full checks are avoided.

questions.question: The UNIX program that checks and repairs file-system consistency after a crash is:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Windows uses chkdsk.

questions.question: Backing up only the files changed since the last full backup is called:
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). A restore needs the full backup plus every incremental backup since.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Linked allocation supports efficient direct access.
II. Indexed allocation supports direct access without external fragmentation.
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Linked allocation needs a pointer chase for direct access.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Contiguous allocation gives fast direct access.
Reason (R): The address of any block can be computed from the starting block and the block number.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Block b + i can be reached directly.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): FAT allocation needs no table in memory.
Reason (R): FAT is a variation of linked allocation.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: The FAT itself is a table, and it is usually cached in memory for speed.

questions.question:
Match the allocation method with its drawback:
a. Contiguous
b. Linked
c. Indexed

1. Slow direct access
2. Index-block overhead for small files
3. External fragmentation
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The basic comparison of allocation methods.

questions.question: Which allocation method was used by the original UNIX file system and ext2/ext3?
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: ext4 adds extents – contiguous runs of blocks.

questions.question: An 'extent' in file systems such as ext4 and NTFS is:

options.B: A contiguous run of blocks described by a start and a length

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Extents reduce metadata and fragmentation for large files.

questions.question: A 'virtual file system' (VFS) layer in an OS allows:

options.A: Different file-system types to be accessed through the same system-call interface
options.B: Files to be stored only in memory

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Linux VFS supports ext4, XFS, NFS, FAT and many others.

questions.question: Which network file system protocol was developed by Sun and is widely used in UNIX/Linux?
questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Windows networks use SMB (CIFS).

questions.question: In a FAT file system, the FAT entry for the last block of a file contains:

options.A: Zero always means the last block
options.C: The first block of the next file

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: Unused blocks are shown by a table value of 0.

questions.question: Defragmentation of a disk mainly helps to:

options.B: Place the blocks of each file contiguously to speed up access

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: SSDs should not be defragmented in the usual way; they use TRIM instead.

questions.question: The counting method of free-space management is efficient when:

options.D: Free blocks occur in contiguous runs

questions.subject: Allocation Methods, Free-space Management, Efficiency and Recovery
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each entry stores the first free block and the number of free blocks following it.

sets.name: 1 · I/O Hardware – Polling, Interrupts, DMA and Memory-mapped I/O

questions.question: The time between the receival of an interrupt and its service is called
questions.subject: I/O Hardware – Polling, Interrupts, DMA and Memory-mapped I/O
questions.explanation: Interrupt latency is the delay from the interrupt request to the start of its service routine. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is TRUE for memory-mapped I/O?

options.A: The I/O devices have separate address space
options.B: The I/O devices and memory share the same address space
options.C: A part of the memory is specially set aside for I/O operation
options.D: The memory and I/O devices have an associated address space

questions.subject: I/O Hardware – Polling, Interrupts, DMA and Memory-mapped I/O
questions.explanation: In memory-mapped I/O, device registers occupy addresses in the same address space as memory and are accessed with ordinary load/store instructions. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Match the following:
a. DRAM
b. DMA
c. Associative mapping
d. Memory-mapped I/O
(i) Offloads data transfer main memory to devices bypassing CPU
(ii) Dynamic memory
(iii) I/O devices treated as memory locations
(iv) Flexible cache mapping by content

options.A: a – i, b – ii, c – iii, d – iv
options.B: a – ii, b – i, c – iv, d – iii
options.C: a – iii, b – iv, c – ii, d – i
options.D: a – iv, b – iii, c – i, d – ii

questions.subject: I/O Hardware – Polling, Interrupts, DMA and Memory-mapped I/O
questions.explanation: DRAM is dynamic memory, DMA bypasses the CPU, associative mapping places blocks anywhere, memory-mapped I/O uses memory addresses for devices. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question:
Consider the following steps in a DMA transfer:
(i) Disk controller initiates DMA transfer
(ii) Disk driver tells disk controller to transfer of bytes from disk to buffer
(iii) Disk controller sends each byte to DMA controller
(iv) Device driver is told to transfer disk data to buffer
Identify the correct sequence.
questions.subject: I/O Hardware – Polling, Interrupts, DMA and Memory-mapped I/O
questions.explanation: Silberschatz's six-step DMA example begins: driver told → driver tells controller → controller initiates DMA → controller sends bytes. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: The DMA read operation transfer data from

options.B: An I/O device to the memory
options.D: An I/O device to CPU register

questions.subject: I/O Hardware – Polling, Interrupts, DMA and Memory-mapped I/O

questions.question:
In the RSA algorithm, let N = P × Q = 33, and let the decryption key D = 7. If the ciphertext corresponds to the letter "E", determine the original plaintext letter.
(Assume A = 1, B = 2, ……, Z = 26).
questions.subject: Program and System Threats, Cryptography and Defences
questions.explanation: M = 5⁷ mod 33: 5² = 25, 5⁴ ≡ 31, 5⁷ ≡ 31 × 25 × 5 = 3875 ≡ 14 → N. (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.question: In a RSA cryptosystem, a participant A uses 2 prime numbers p = 13 and q = 17, to generate public and private keys if the public key of A is 35, then private key of A is

options.A: Private key of participant A = (d, n) = (11, 192)
options.B: Private key of participant A = (d, n) = (11, 221)
options.C: Private key of participant A = (d, n) = (7, 220)
options.D: Private key of participant A = (d, n) = (10, 195)

questions.subject: Program and System Threats, Cryptography and Defences
questions.explanation: n = 13 × 17 = 221, φ(n) = 12 × 16 = 192, and 35 × 11 = 385 = 2 × 192 + 1, so d = 11 and the private key is (11, 221). (Answer worked out by ExamSim; not KEA's official key.)

questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). WannaCry (2017) was a major ransomware worm.

questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Signature-based IDS look for known patterns; anomaly-based IDS look for unusual behaviour.

questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching
questions.explanation: Others include performance, international support, energy efficiency and dynamic device support.

questions.question: The Windows layer that hides differences between hardware chipsets from the kernel is the:

questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching
questions.explanation: The executive runs above the kernel and the HAL.

questions.question: The Windows component that checks every access to an object against its access-control list is the:
questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching

questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching

options.B: Run Linux command-line tools and distributions on Windows

questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Virtualisation-based security also uses it.

questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching

options.A: Several users to stay logged on, switching between sessions without closing programs

questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). Each user gets a separate session; it is built on Terminal Services technology.

options.C: Run a desktop session on a remote Windows computer over the network

questions.subject: Design Principles, System Components, Terminal Services and Fast User Switching
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KEA / KSET papers). The client program is mstsc.exe.
